_comment: How Persian's phrases hold together, for lib/chunker.py. Optional, like every file of this name.
_np_head: Persian puts the noun first and its adjectives after it (کتابِ بزرگ), so a modifier attaches BACK to the noun it follows, not forward to one it precedes.
_adposition: به خانه, در تاریکی, از او: a preposition binds forward to its object and is meaningless without it. را is the one that goes the other way, and it is a particle, which the rules attach backwards already.
_verb_final: The verb comes last: a noun before a verb is its object and leans toward it, and a noun after a finished verb begins a new clause.
_bind_forward: THE EZAFE, which this toolbox's texts mark as a kasra on the GOVERNING word (docs/lang/fa.md). A word carrying it is not finished: what it governs is in the next word, and the ezafe that is easiest to lose is exactly the one whose qualifier falls into the next chunk.

function_words._comment: The closed classes, which the dictionary is the wrong authority on: it files می under a conjunction and آن with more senses as a noun. می and نمی are the verb's own prefixes written apart (PREF): they bind to the verb after them, and the seam before them is the seam before that verb. را, the plural ها and the enclitics written apart (PART) lean on the word before them. The forms are compared with the harakat and the joiners taken off, as the dictionary is searched, so a vowelled text reads the same.

_closing: The particle that CLOSES the phrase it ends: the object marker. After it the phrase is done, and the seam is a cut (تَروُ خُشک را | مِثلِ ایران).
_question_words: The words that open a question. tidy.py ends a sentence holding one of these with ؟ rather than a full stop, which is all they are used for: an automatic transcript prints no punctuation at all, and a question that looks like a statement reads as one. آیا is unambiguous; the rest ask in every position they stand in here.
_question_any: ...and of those, the ones that can ONLY ask: a question particle, which means a question wherever in the sentence it stands. The rest are read at the edges alone, because they mean other things in the middle of one.
_question_mark: the stop a question takes, and the one a statement takes
_light_verbs: The light verbs of a compound verb (docs/lang/fa.md: never split one): کردن شدن دادن زدن گرفتن and the rest, in any person and with their prefixes. A noun or adjective before one is the verb's own half -- فکر کردن, دوست داشتن, صحبت می‌کردیم -- matched on a word the dictionary calls a verb, or does not know.
